business_rules_enhanced.rule_description: After 5 consecutive failed login attempts, user account is locked for 15 minutes
business_rules_enhanced.confidence_rationale: Explicit code with named constants confirms rule
business_rules_enhanced.business_impact: Prevents brute-force password attacks while allowing legitimate users to regain access after timeout
business_rules_enhanced.regulatory_context: Aligns with NIST SP 800-63B authentication guidelines
business_rules_enhanced.implementation_notes: Lockout counter resets on successful login. Admin can manually unlock accounts.
business_rules_enhanced.business_objective: Prevent automated brute-force password attacks while maintaining user accessibility through temporary lockout mechanism. Balances security requirements with user experience.
business_rules_enhanced.business_terminology: When a user fails to log in 5 times in a row, the system temporarily blocks their account for 15 minutes to protect against automated password guessing attacks. After 15 minutes, the user can try again. This prevents hackers from trying thousands of password combinations while allowing real users to regain access quickly.
business_rules_enhanced.regulatory_rationale: Implements NIST SP 800-63B Section 5.2.2 requirements for authentication rate limiting and account lockout to prevent online guessing attacks. Aligns with PCI DSS Requirement 8.1.6 for limiting repeated access attempts.

enhancement_sources.business_objective: security-policy-specialist: NIST SP 800-63B authentication security guidance
enhancement_sources.stakeholder_owner: Derived from rule category (security) mapping to IT Security Department
enhancement_sources.regulatory_rationale: security-policy-specialist: NIST SP 800-63B Section 5.2.2 and PCI DSS 8.1.6

business_rules_enhanced.rule_description: Failed login attempt counter resets to 0 after successful login
business_rules_enhanced.business_impact: Prevents permanent lockout for users who occasionally mistype passwords
business_rules_enhanced.business_objective: Allow users who successfully authenticate to start with clean slate, preventing accumulation of old failed attempts that could lead to unnecessary lockouts
business_rules_enhanced.business_terminology: Once a user successfully logs in, the system forgets all previous failed login attempts. This means occasional typos or forgotten passwords won't accumulate over time and eventually lock out the user.
business_rules_enhanced.regulatory_rationale: Supports NIST SP 800-63B usability requirements by not penalizing users for historical failed attempts after successful authentication

business_rules_enhanced.rule_description: Passwords must be at least 8 characters and include uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character
business_rules_enhanced.confidence_rationale: Explicit regex pattern confirms all complexity requirements
business_rules_enhanced.business_impact: Enforces strong password policy to prevent easy-to-guess passwords
business_rules_enhanced.business_objective: Enforce strong password creation to protect customer accounts from compromise due to weak, easily guessable passwords. Reduces risk of account takeover and unauthorized access to sensitive customer data.
business_rules_enhanced.business_terminology: When creating a new password, users must include a mix of uppercase letters (A-Z), lowercase letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and special characters (!@#$%, etc.) with a minimum length of 8 characters. This makes passwords harder to guess and protects accounts from hackers.

stakeholder_owner.decision_authority: IT Security Department with Data Protection Officer approval

business_rules_enhanced.regulatory_rationale: Implements NIST SP 800-63B Section 5.1.1 password composition requirements. Supports GDPR Article 32 requirement for appropriate technical measures to ensure data security.

enhancement_sources.stakeholder_owner: Derived from rule category (validation) and security context
enhancement_sources.regulatory_rationale: security-policy-specialist: NIST SP 800-63B Section 5.1.1 and GDPR Article 32

business_rules_enhanced.rule_description: Passwords must be hashed using bcrypt algorithm with cost factor 12 before database storage
business_rules_enhanced.confidence_rationale: Explicit use of bcrypt library with cost factor
business_rules_enhanced.business_impact: Protects passwords even if database is compromised
business_rules_enhanced.regulatory_context: Industry best practice for password storage
business_rules_enhanced.business_objective: Ensure customer passwords remain secure even if database is breached. One-way hashing prevents password recovery by attackers who gain database access, protecting customer accounts across all systems where they may reuse passwords.
business_rules_enhanced.business_terminology: The system never stores actual passwords. Instead, it converts passwords into a scrambled format (hash) using a secure algorithm that cannot be reversed. Even if someone steals the database, they cannot recover the original passwords.

stakeholder_owner.business_owner: Data Protection Officer and IT Security Department

business_rules_enhanced.regulatory_rationale: Implements NIST SP 800-63B Section 5.1.1.2 requirement for approved password hashing algorithms. Aligns with GDPR Article 32 requirement for pseudonymization and encryption of personal data. Satisfies PCI DSS Requirement 8.2.1 for rendering authentication credentials unreadable.

enhancement_sources.business_objective: security-policy-specialist: Password storage security best practices
enhancement_sources.stakeholder_owner: Data Protection Officer ownership derived from GDPR compliance requirements
enhancement_sources.regulatory_rationale: security-policy-specialist: NIST, OWASP, PCI DSS password storage standards

business_rules_enhanced.rule_description: Upon successful credential validation, a new session token must be created with 30-minute expiration and stored in session database
business_rules_enhanced.confidence_rationale: Explicit session creation with timeout configuration
business_rules_enhanced.business_impact: Enables stateful user sessions for authenticated requests without re-authentication
business_rules_enhanced.business_objective: Enable seamless user experience by maintaining authentication state across multiple requests without requiring users to re-enter credentials for each action. Balances usability with security through time-limited sessions.
business_rules_enhanced.business_terminology: After successfully logging in, the system gives the user a temporary access pass (session) that lasts for 30 minutes. This allows the user to navigate the application and perform actions without logging in again for each page. The session automatically expires after 30 minutes of inactivity for security.

stakeholder_owner.business_owner: User Experience Team and IT Security Department (shared)

business_rules_enhanced.regulatory_rationale: Supports NIST SP 800-63B Section 7.2 session management requirements including timeout for inactivity. Aligns with SOC 2 CC6.1 for logical access security.

enhancement_sources.business_objective: Derived from rule category (integration) and session management context
enhancement_sources.stakeholder_owner: Shared ownership: UX team (experience) and IT Security (timeout policy)
enhancement_sources.regulatory_rationale: security-policy-specialist: NIST SP 800-63B Section 7.2 and SOC 2 CC6.1

business_rules_enhanced.rule_description: Sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity. Active sessions renew timeout automatically with each request.
business_rules_enhanced.confidence_rationale: Clear logic from code structure, implementation confirms timeout renewal
business_rules_enhanced.business_impact: Protects inactive sessions from unauthorized use while minimizing user re-authentication burden
business_rules_enhanced.business_objective: Automatically terminate inactive user sessions to prevent unauthorized access if user walks away from computer, while keeping active users logged in for continuous work without interruption
business_rules_enhanced.business_terminology: If a user is actively using the application, their session stays alive and they remain logged in. However, if the user is inactive for 30 minutes (no clicks, no page loads), the system automatically logs them out to protect their account if they forgot to log out or left their computer unattended.
business_rules_enhanced.regulatory_rationale: Implements NIST SP 800-63B Section 7.2 requirement for reauthentication after period of inactivity. Supports SOC 2 CC6.1 logical access security controls for automatic session termination.

enhancement_sources.stakeholder_owner: Derived from rule category (security) and session management
enhancement_sources.regulatory_rationale: security-policy-specialist: NIST SP 800-63B Section 7.2 and SOC 2

business_rules_enhanced.rule_description: Corporate user accounts must authenticate against enterprise LDAP directory using LDAPS protocol
business_rules_enhanced.confidence_rationale: Explicit LDAP integration for corporate accounts
business_rules_enhanced.business_impact: Enables single sign-on for corporate users, centralizes credential management
business_rules_enhanced.user_feedback: LDAP authentication is required by our enterprise security policy, not just implementation choice
business_rules_enhanced.business_objective: Enable corporate employees to use their existing company credentials (same username/password they use for email, network login, etc.) to access the application. Centralizes user management in IT department and ensures consistent security policies across all corporate systems.
business_rules_enhanced.business_terminology: Corporate employees log in using their company credentials (the same ones they use for email and network access). The system checks these credentials against the company's central user directory (LDAP) rather than maintaining separate passwords. This provides single sign-on convenience and centralized security management.

stakeholder_owner.technical_owner: Authentication Services Team and Directory Services Team (shared)

business_rules_enhanced.regulatory_rationale: Enterprise Security Policy mandates LDAP authentication for all corporate users to ensure centralized credential management, consistent password policies, and compliance with SOC 2 CC6.1 logical access requirements. LDAPS (LDAP over SSL) required for encryption of credentials in transit per Enterprise Network Security Policy.

enhancement_sources.business_objective: User feedback: Enterprise security policy mandate for centralized authentication
enhancement_sources.regulatory_rationale: User feedback: Enterprise SSO Policy requirement and security-policy-specialist for SOC 2 context

business_processes.process_description: Complete workflow for user login, session creation, and session management. Ensures only authorized users access the system while maintaining seamless user experience through persistent sessions.

process_steps.step_description: System validates username and password against stored credentials (or LDAP for corporate users). Failed attempts are tracked to prevent brute-force attacks.
process_steps.business_rationale: Ensures only authorized users access the system and protects against automated password guessing attacks
process_steps.stakeholder_value: Protects customer data and prevents unauthorized access while allowing legitimate users to authenticate efficiently

process_steps.step_description: Upon successful validation, system creates secure session token with 30-minute expiration and stores in session database
process_steps.business_rationale: Enables stateful user interactions without re-authentication for each request
process_steps.stakeholder_value: Improves user experience through persistent login sessions while maintaining security

process_steps.step_description: System monitors session validity, handles timeouts (30 minutes inactivity), and manages session renewal on user activity
process_steps.business_rationale: Balances security (automatic logout of inactive sessions) with usability (session renewal on activity)
process_steps.stakeholder_value: Protects inactive sessions from unauthorized use while minimizing user re-authentication burden

business_processes.process_owner: IT Security Department and Authentication Services Team

business_processes.process_description: Workflow for password policy enforcement, password validation, hashing, and secure storage. Ensures all passwords meet security requirements and are stored securely.

process_steps.step_description: System validates password meets minimum complexity requirements (8+ characters, uppercase, lowercase, number, special character)
process_steps.business_rationale: Enforces strong password policy to prevent easy-to-guess passwords that could be cracked by attackers
process_steps.stakeholder_value: Protects customer accounts from unauthorized access due to weak passwords

process_steps.step_description: System hashes password using bcrypt algorithm (cost factor 12) before storing in database. Original password never stored.
process_steps.business_rationale: Protects passwords even if database is compromised through one-way hashing that cannot be reversed
process_steps.stakeholder_value: Ensures customer credentials remain secure even in database breach scenarios

business_processes.process_owner: IT Security Department and Data Protection Officer

business_terms.definition: A unique identifier generated by the system after successful user login, allowing the user to access protected resources without re-authenticating for each request
business_terms.technical_equivalent: JWT (JSON Web Token) or session ID stored in session database
business_terms.business_context: Enables seamless user experience - user logs in once and can navigate the entire application for 30 minutes without entering password again. Similar to a temporary access badge that expires.

business_terms.definition: Temporary suspension of login capability for a user account after repeated failed authentication attempts
business_terms.business_context: Security measure to prevent automated password guessing attacks (brute-force). Temporarily blocks account for 15 minutes after 5 failed attempts, then allows user to try again.

business_terms.definition: One-way cryptographic transformation of a password into a scrambled format that cannot be reversed to recover the original password
business_terms.business_context: Protects customer passwords even if someone steals the database. The system never stores actual passwords, only hashed versions. This prevents password recovery by attackers.

business_terms.definition: Automatic expiration of a user's login session after a period of inactivity (30 minutes)
business_terms.business_context: Security feature that logs users out automatically if they leave their computer unattended. Prevents unauthorized access if user forgets to log out. Active users remain logged in indefinitely as long as they continue using the system.

business_terms.definition: Verification of user credentials against a centralized enterprise directory server using LDAP protocol
business_terms.technical_equivalent: ldapService.authenticate(username, password) against enterprise Active Directory
business_terms.business_context: Allows corporate employees to use their company credentials (same as email/network login) for single sign-on. Centralizes user management in IT department and ensures consistent password policies.

business_terms.definition: Automated attempt to guess user passwords by trying many combinations in rapid succession
business_terms.technical_equivalent: Automated scripts sending multiple authentication requests with different password guesses
business_terms.business_context: Account lockout rule (AUTH-BR-001) protects against this attack type by limiting login attempts and introducing delays, making password guessing impractical for attackers.

technical_terms_translated.business_description: System component that validates user credentials (username and password) against stored values or LDAP directory
System component that generates and stores session tokens after successful login

recommendations: All 7 rules successfully enhanced with business context and stakeholder ownership - ready for stakeholder presentation
Business processes BP-AUTH-001 and BP-PASSWORD-001 are both Critical priority - prioritize in migration planning and ensure zero downtime during transition
IT Security Department and Data Protection Officer should jointly review enhanced security and password rules (AUTH-BR-001, AUTH-BR-005, AUTH-BR-006) for final approval
Customer Service Department requires training on enhanced authentication policies before migration - particularly account lockout procedures and password complexity requirements
Consider stakeholder workshop with IT Security, DPO, and UX Team to validate business objectives and discuss potential usability improvements (e.g., adjusting lockout duration from 15 to 10 minutes)
High confidence in all technical rules (6 rules at score 5, 1 rule at score 4) - technical accuracy validated in Phase 3
Enterprise LDAP integration (AUTH-BR-020) flagged as mandatory requirement - ensure LDAP availability and failover procedures in VNRM migration design (Phase 5)
Glossary successfully translates 6 business terms and 5 technical terms - suitable for stakeholder documentation and training materials
